scope: Independent source-only review of root-authored common, watchdog, launcher and protocol; adjacent input/reader interfaces inspected for compatibility.
checks: Single execution/attempt.json, same monitor identity/PID namespace, owned child session and fixed thread environment agree between common, run and inherited watchdog.

The 97 ordered fixed rows comprise three complete 32-row populations plus AO. Five worlds and 32 seeds imply 15520 research lives, four retained startup lives and 15524 total calls; four groups times five worlds imply twenty raw/scored batches and 485 genome/world rows.

Runtime caps are 2640 CPU and 1740 wall seconds with one two-thread worker; full 60 CPU/60 wall reserve yields the stated 2700/1800 package cap. Owned RSS, address-space, host floor and cleanup limits are passed unchanged to the watchdog.

Launcher and measurement complete markers agree exactly on twelve fields. Worker writes and validates raw/scored batches, performs saved-data analysis before successful exit, then the monitor checks hashes and cleared ownership before terminal completion.

The reused accounting reconstruct and describe functions use supplied row length. New analyzer does not call the old four-role/512-life analysis entrypoint. Cartesian genotype-major batch flattening is split consistently into 32-life rows.

Input/source/production pins, namespace receipt/reservation pins, prospective publication commit/manifest, actual-input review and release/attempt provenance connect through the current single-worker paths.

The protocol treats all five worlds and the full panel as development evidence, retains duplicates, uses seed-level population uncertainty, labels fresh joint ranks descriptive and does not replace historical endpoints.
limits: No materialized protocol or input arrays existed at review time; exact actual-input and namespace acceptance remains a separate prelaunch check.
This review establishes source/interface consistency, not empirical worker execution, runtime sufficiency or an independent reimplementation of the inherited accounting reducer.
